texts.exact_text: Yü indicates that, (in the state which it implies), feudal princes may be set up, and the hosts put in motion, with advantage.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, hexagram statement
texts.notes: Legge's title restored from the source statement.

texts.exact_text: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject proclaiming his pleasure and satisfaction. There will be evil.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second SIX, divided, shows one who is firm as a rock. (He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of pleasure and satisfaction. If he would understand! -- If he be late in doing so, there will indeed be occasion for repentance.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom the harmony and satisfaction come. Great is the success which he obtains. Let him not allow suspicions to enter his mind, and thus friends will gather around him.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth six, divided, shows one with a chronic complaint, but who lives on without dying.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost six, divided, shows its subject with darkened mind devoted to the pleasure and satisfaction (of the time); but if he change his course even when (it may be considered as) completed, there will be no error.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, line 6

texts.exact_text:
The hexagram Yü denoted to king Wén a condition of harmony and happy contentment throughout the kingdom, when the people rejoiced in and readily obeyed their sovereign. At such a time his appointments and any military undertakings would be hailed and supported. The fourth line, undivided, is the lord of the figure, and being close to the fifth or place of dignity, is to be looked on as the minister or chief officer of the ruler. The ruler gives to him his confidence; and all represented by the other lines yield their obedience.

Line 1 is weak, and has for its correlate the strong 4. Its subject may well enjoy the happiness of the time. But he cannot contain himself, and proclaims, or boasts of, his satisfaction; -- which is evil.

Line 2, though weak, is in its correct position, the centre, moreover, of the lower trigram. Quietly and firmly its subject is able to abide in his place, and exercise a far-seeing discrimination. All is indicative of good fortune.

Line 3 is weak, and in an odd place. Immediately below line 4, its subject keeps looking up to the lord of the figure, and depends on him, thinking of doing nothing, but how to enjoy himself. The consequence will be as described, unless he speedily change.

The strong subject of line 4 is the agent to whom the happy condition is owing; and it is only necessary to caution him to maintain his confidence in himself and his purpose, and his adherents and success will continue.

Line 5 is in the ruler's place; but it is weak, and he is in danger of being carried away by the lust of pleasure. Moreover, proximity to the powerful minister represented by 4 is a source of danger. Hence he is represented as suffering from a chronic complaint, but nevertheless he does not die. See Appendix II on the line.

Line 6, at the very top or end of the hexagram, is weak, and its subject is all but lost. Still even for him there is a chance of safety, if he will but change. 豫 ䷏
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 16; scan-backed transcription p. 91, notes

texts.exact_text: 豫：利建侯行師。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 豫，剛應而志行，順以動，豫。豫，順以動，故天地如之，而況建侯行師乎？天地以順動，故日月不過，而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 彖

texts.exact_text: 雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初六：鳴豫，凶。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 初六鳴豫，志窮凶也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 六二：介于石，不終日，貞吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 不終日，貞吉；以中正也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 六三：盱豫，悔。遲有悔。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 盱豫有悔，位不當也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 九四：由豫，大有得。勿疑。朋盍簪。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 由豫，大有得；志大行也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 六五：貞疾，恆不死。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 六五貞疾，乘剛也。恆不死，中未亡也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上六：冥豫，成有渝，无咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/豫; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 16, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 冥豫在上，何可長也。

texts.exact_text:
In Yü we see the strong (line) responded to by all the others, and the will (of him whom it represents) being carried out; and (also) docile obedience employing movement (for its purposes). (From these things comes) Yü (the Condition of harmony and satisfaction).

In this condition we have docile obedience employing movement (for its purposes), and therefore it is so as between heaven and earth; -- how much more will it be so (among men) in 'the setting up of feudal princes and putting the hosts in motion!'

Heaven and earth show that docile obedience in connexion with movement, and hence the sun and moon make no error (in time), and the four seasons do not deviate (from their order). The sages show such docile obedience in connexion with their movements, and hence their punishments and penalties are entirely just, and the people acknowledge it by their submission. Great indeed are the time and significance indicated in Yü!
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 16, p. 228

texts.exact_text: (The trigrams ☷ ☳ for) the earth and thunder issuing from it with its crashing noise form Yü. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, composed their music and did honour to virtue, presenting it especially and most grandly to God, when they associated with Him (at the service) their highest ancestor and their father.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, p. 288

texts.exact_text: 'The (subject of the) first six proclaims his pleasure and satisfaction:' -- there will be evil; his wishes have been satisfied to overflowing.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 1, p. 288

texts.exact_text: '(He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune:' -- this is shown by the central and correct position (of the line).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 2, p. 288

texts.exact_text: 'He looks up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of satisfaction; there will be occasion for repentance:' -- this is intimated by the position not being the appropriate one.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 3, p. 288

texts.exact_text: 'From him the harmony and satisfaction come; great is the success which he obtains:' -- his aims take effect on a grand scale.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 4, p. 288

texts.exact_text: '(The subject of) the fifth six has a chronic complaint:' -- this is shown by his being mounted on the strong (line). 'He still lives on without dying:' -- he is in the central position, (and its memories of the past) have not yet perished.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 5, p. 288

texts.exact_text: 'With darkened mind devoted to the harmony and satisfaction (of the time),' as shown in the topmost (line): -- how can one in such a condition continue long?
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 16, line 6, p. 288
